source.original_data: Figshare DOI 10.17045/STHLMUNI.14260211, article 14260211, Audusseau_etal2021_batch_monitoring.csv, file ID 29157873

question: Can recent preceding Araschnia levana presence at a site explain a resident butterfly's subsequent Sturmia bella parasitism beyond contemporaneous co-occurrence, phenology, butterfly density, county and year?
introduced_herbivore: Araschnia levana (northward range expanding in Sweden, using the existing resident Urtica dioica host)
parasitoid: Sturmia bella (microtype eggs on nettle leaves, can be acquired after sampling through lab-supplied local leaves)
baseline: Same-batch larval instar, resident species, year, county, study week and week squared, latitude, contemporaneous Araschnia presence, log1p(current total observed larvae), log1p(previous site-week total observed larvae), elapsed survey weeks.
incremental_predictor: binary Araschnia levana observed at the immediately previous survey occasion within 1–3 weeks in the SAME site and SAME year (excluding current and future rows); if prior encounter absent because no sampling, exclude not impute zero
primary_outcome: Within the collected resident-butterfly larvae from each sampled batch, observed reared Sturmia bella emerging during larval or pupal stages (sum corresponding count fields only if non-overlapping per protocol source; total ≤ nb_larvae_in_lab). Observation proxy for parasitoid attack, NOT demonstrated in-field transmission or viable adult recruitment.
time_alignment: Within each site BMS_id × year, aggregate source batches into site×ISO-week observations. Use actual Araschnia levana butterfly species presence/abundance rather than a recipient's parasite outcome to define exposure. Require previous sampled week gap 1–3, never connect across years.
primary_evaluation: Leave-one-original-site (BMS_id) out across both years, train on other sites; mean heldout binomial logloss per original butterfly larva; report baseline minus lag-augmented logloss; site-cluster bootstrap CI 2000 draws, seed 20261010. Validates prediction transport between sampled sites, not time-forward causal effects.

requirements.source_sturmia_species_count_consistency: sum of original two resident butterflies close to published 39 and 105, with transparent mismatches

sensitivity: Same source years independently (2017 / 2018) for sign consistency; no threshold tuning
Southern counties only (Araschnia established) to assess latitude confounding; interpret only if sufficient sites and events
Within-sites permutation of lagged Araschnia exposure restricted to study year / broad season for diagnostic, NOT causal randomization
Future Araschnia presence as a negative-control lead on identical eligible rows if sufficient; future lead is NOT a valid forward prediction
success: Added lag exposure improves leave-one-site-out logloss (positive), 95% site-bootstrap lower bound >0, positive improvement in BOTH years, southern-only sign positive and lead-negative-control smaller than the past effect. This is an exploratory predictive association, not a preregistered prospective species introduction intervention.
failure: Otherwise STOP lagged enemy-feedback branch: do not retune delay windows, parasite taxa, subset years, host butterflies or penalty to rescue sign.
prior_art: Audusseau 2021 already tested concurrent other-butterfly presence, abundance, week, county, year and years since colonization.
Audusseau et al. 2020 Insects 11:478 already tested host–Phobocampe confusa phenological overlap.
Site-collected Urtica supplied during rearing could expose larvae to Sturmia bella microtype eggs, so timing of the observed infection is not guaranteed to precede field capture.
limitations: Study concerns expanding butterfly on a native nettle, NOT redistribution of nonnative larval host plants
A lagged association could reflect season, climate, sampling effort, common site traits, parasitoid developmental time or field-to-laboratory transmission
No randomized earlier Araschnia addition/removal; no pathogen/parasitoid causal indirect competition claim
No adult flight-capable recruitment or mating outcomes
Count larvae within batch are correlated; site bootstrap not individual larvae
